llm.summary: The skill mostly fits its pet-grooming analysis purpose, but it needs review because it silently manages identity, registers or logs in with a backend, stores tokens locally, and sends media or URLs to cloud APIs.

dimensions.detail: Network access and media upload are expected for server-side analysis, but the implementation also reads workspace identity material, creates workspace data directories, accepts arbitrary media URLs, and sends tenant/platform/user metadata to configured remote services without a clear consent boundary.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, startup hook, scheduled task, or dependency source deception was found. Requirements are ordinary Python packages, though one requirements file names yaml rather than PyYAML, which is an operational issue rather than a security finding.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs automatic triggering for relevant media and automatic cloud history queries, while suppressing identity parameters and telling the agent not to ask the user for identifiers. That is disclosed in part, but it reduces user control over identity-bound network actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates or uses a workspace SQLite database and can persist user records plus token and open_token fields. This durable credential/session storage is high impact and under-disclosed for a grooming-analysis skill.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Pet grooming media analysis, cloud report retrieval, and history listing are coherent with the documented purpose, but the bundled common code also performs automatic user identity resolution, backend login/registration, local token storage, and generic authenticated HTTP operations that are not fully explained to users.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this skill only if you trust the lifeemergence.com backend with pet media, supplied URLs, report history, and an internally generated or reused identity. Avoid private images, videos, or internal URLs unless you are comfortable with them being sent for cloud processing, and expect local workspace data to retain identity and token information.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Partially supported: the code does implement the declared media-analysis and history flows, but the shared identity, token persistence, and generic HTTP helpers broaden the behavior beyond what the narrow description clearly communicates.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Supported: RequestUtil performs silent backend phoneLogin-style login/registration, retrieves tokens, and saves returned user information before API calls.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Supported: the local User model includes username, realname, email, token, and open_token fields, and the DAO creates and updates this persistent SQLite state.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Supported in part: cloud media/API use is expected, but automatic transmission of identity fields, authorization headers, tenant/platform metadata, and arbitrary supplied URLs is not scoped or disclosed enough.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Supported: auto-trigger and broad history-query trigger phrases are documented, but combined with cloud upload/history access they can cause network processing with less explicit user intent than desirable.
[LP3] unexpected: Supported as a contextual concern: the skill relies on filesystem, network, and script execution behavior without explicit permission scoping metadata; this is not malicious by itself but compounds the identity and persistence concerns.
[YR4] expected: Downgraded: manual inspection found the zero-width joiners in visible emoji sequences, not hidden manifest instructions or metadata poisoning.
[P9] expected: Downgraded: the whitespace padding appears to be ordinary Python line wrapping around a conditional expression, with no hidden instruction content nearby.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded for security verdict: Chinese-language strings and docs are visible and consistent with the bilingual/Chinese artifact, and did not drive the Review verdict.
[A.I.G SARIF] expected: The supplied A.I.G scan reported no results, which did not override the artifact-backed identity, persistence, and network-transparency concerns.
